subject: Edge deployment: VPC traffic segmentation & nodepool guidance
messages:
From: Paul Rowan <paul.rowan@nimhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Edge cluster + VPC review request

Jonas,

Thanks for taking a look. We're scoping a private Kubernetes deployment to host Redwood inference instances at three of our clinic sites. High level constraints:
- Each site: 2 x GPU servers (A100-class), 6 x CPU-only nodes for preprocessing and sidecars.
- All traffic must traverse our on-prem network and egress through a central NAT gateway into our VPC (no direct internet from nodes).
- Storage: patient data must be encrypted at rest; model artifacts can be cached on local NVMe.
- We need predictable egress IPs for allowlisting with third-party telemetry and S3 endpoints.

Can you advise on how to structure node pools (serving, batch, infra), how to do network segmentation inside the VPC, and any gotchas for storage classes / CSI drivers? Attached is a minimal inventory.

[Attachment: env-inventory.csv (CSV, 18KB)]

Would prefer a 30–45 minute workshop to walk through options next week.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Rowan
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Health

Paul — thanks for the inventory and the constraints, helpful. Quick confirmation questions before the workshop:
- Do all three sites need identical node pools, or can we vary by site (e.g., one site as primary with larger GPU headroom)?
- Which on-prem networking hardware are you using for the WAN? Is it BGP-capable for potential BGP-peering to the VPC edge?
- Do you require FIPS / HSM-backed KMS for encryption keys, or is KMS with customer-managed keys in the cloud acceptable?

I propose a 45-minute cadence: 30 minutes discovery + 15 minutes to agree actions. We have slots Mon/Tue morning PT. Laura and Irene will join for storage and networking specifics.

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed layout for Nimbus on-prem clusters (draft)

Team — following Tue's workshop with Paul, below is a draft deployment pattern for Nimbus. This is an internal working note I will share with the customer after feedback. Please review and call out any hard blockers.

Summary of agreed constraints:
- Three sites: site-a (primary), site-b (primary), site-c (DR smaller).
- On-prem network: Arista spine/leaf, BGP-capable to VPC edge.
- HSM on-prem for patient data encryption; model cache may use cloud KMS via peered VPC.

High-level cluster composition (per site):
- Control plane: 3 x small VMs (HA), run as dedicated control-plane on internal management VLAN; no GPUs.
- GPU serving pool (gpserve): 2 nodes (site-c: 1 node), tainted for model-serving workloads, autoscaler disabled (manual scaling for predictability).
- Preproc/batch pool (batch): 4–6 CPU nodes with larger ephemeral SSDs (for transforms, batch offline jobs); use Cluster Autoscaler with conservative scale-up.
- Infra/system pool (infra): 2 nodes for logging/metrics/sidecars, run kube-proxy, calico nodes; smaller instance types.

Storage strategy:
- Local NVMe (scratch) for tokenizers and model caches. Use ephemeral local-storage CSI driver with eviction policy for cache artifacts.
- Block storage for persistent volumes: RBD (Ceph) or enterprise SAN presented as iSCSI with multipath. All PVs for patient data must be encrypted with HSM-backed keys (on-prem KMS)/KMS sharding.
- Shared NFS for cross-pod small-volume artifacts (non-sensitive).
- Storage classes: nvme-fast (ephemeral), block-encrypted (RBD/iSCSI + CSI with encryption), nfs-shared.

Networking & routing:
- Segmentation: management VLAN (control plane), data VLAN (pods), ingress/edge VLAN (ingress controllers & NAT).
- Egress design: all node egress NAT through on-prem NAT gateway -> transit to VPC egress via IPSEC/BGP. Use dedicated egress IPs per site and register them as allowlisted addresses.
- Service mesh: optional — prefer not for first-phase; use strict NetworkPolicies scoped to namespaces instead.
- External endpoints (S3, telemetry): prefer private VPC endpoints, otherwise route through controlled NAT with TLS inspection as required.

Operational controls & SLOs:
- PodDisruptionBudgets on serving deployments to retain minimum replicas.
- Use pre-stop hooks + PDB-aware draining to avoid eviction of GPU workloads during maintenance.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching at runtime to avoid repeated PK loads across replicas.

Rollout plan (canary first site):
1) Provision control plane + infra pools in site-a; smoke test with non-prod models.
2) Deploy gpserve pool and run small-scale load test (10 qps) and storage IO baseline.
3) Validate egress IP allowlisting and KMS integration.
4) Repeat for site-b; site-c is DR with single-node gpserve.

Known risks / notes:
- HSM integration will require network reachability from control-plane or a secure proxy. We need the exact HSM model to confirm driver support.
- Autoscaler behavior with taints/tolerations: cluster-autoscaler should be restricted to batch pool to avoid scaling GPUs unexpectedly.
- Local NVMe eviction + model cache priming needs an init job to prefetch warm models.

Attachments: initial-sizing.xlsx (workload assumptions, cost delta scenarios), proposed-network-diagram.png

Action items:
- Vivek: validate BGP peering feasibility and required firewall ACLs for site->VPC (due Thu).
- Irene: confirm CSI driver choices and encryption plugin compatibility with Nimbus HSM (due Fri).
- Laura: finalize PV reclaim policy recommendations and backup cadence (due Fri).

If no major objections I will package this and send to Paul with a short executive summary and a DocuSign approval link for the next-phase work order.

Jonas

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed layout for Nimbus on-prem clusters (draft)

Jonas — good draft, a few clarifications and suggestions:
- Taints/tolerations: specify "gpserve:NoSchedule" and only add tolerations to the model-serving deployments. Add a separate NodeAffinity for GPU SKU to make scheduling deterministic.
- CSI drivers: prefer RBD (Ceph) where available; otherwise use iSCSI with multipathd. For encryption, the CSI secrets-store-provider should be the on-prem HSM proxy — avoid direct KMS calls from nodes.
- Consider using local-lvm for ephemeral scratch to control thin provisioning and reduce noisy-neighbor IO spikes.
- Add a Persistent Volume for model-artifact manifests (small) on encrypted block so redeploys don't need to re-prime caches.

I'll take the action to prototype a small Ceph-backed PV with on-prem KMS integration and report back.

Irene
Senior Storage Engineer — Redwood Inference
